188: 
189: ### Performance

191: 
192: ### Security
193: - **NFR-S01**: No brief or script in this phase carries a credential, token or key. The only model call is the read-only frontier review.

196: - **NFR-R01**: Every number is computed by a command in `tasks.md`, so a second conductor gets the same numbers from the same tree.

201:

203: - Empty input: a doc with no `Status` row counts as not Draft, so its tokens are errors.
204: - Maximum length: a stamp is read only from the first 70 lines of a doc.
205: 
206: ### Error Scenarios
207: - External service failure: if the frontier review cannot run, the conductor records the error and leaves REQ-009 open.
208: - Network timeout: not applicable, no step uses the network except the review.
209: - Stale build: `validate.sh` refuses to run on a stale `dist/` and exits 3, so a missing rebuild shows as a clear error and not as a wrong verdict.

240: ### US-001: Leftover hints are caught (Priority: P0)
241: 
242: **As a** reviewer of a DeepSeek-authored packet, **I want** a leftover template hint to fail validation once the packet leaves Draft, **so that** an unfinished packet cannot pass as finished.
243: 
244: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).

249: 
250: **As the** operator of an external repo, **I want** my existing packets to validate exactly as before, **so that** `/doctor:update` does not turn a green tree red.
251: 
252: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).

56: ## 3. ARCHITECTURE
57: 
58: ### Pattern
59: A stamp-gated lifecycle. The template stamp says which contract a doc was written under. The validator keeps the old strict verdict for any doc without the new stamp and applies the Draft lifecycle only to docs that carry it.
60: 
61: ### Facts read from the tree while this plan was written
62: 
63: - `validate.sh` runs the compiled `runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`, never the shell rules, for the rule `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The orchestrator lists it in `nativeRuleIds`, and `runRegistryShellRules` skips every rule in that set. The proof is the wording: a v2.3 scaffold validated in a scratch copy printed `unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet`, which is the new orchestrator message, and not the shell message.
64: - `validate.sh` exits 3 with the text `compiled validation orchestrator is stale` when `runtime/dist` is older than its source. So the TypeScript edit is invisible until `npm run build` runs under `runtime/`.
65: - `rules/check-placeholders.sh` still matters. The harness `runtime/cli/tests/test-validation-extended.sh` sources it in the category `Individual Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED (check-placeholders.sh)`, and its header says it mirrors the orchestrator.
66: - A warning does not fail strict. The orchestrator sets `passed: summary.errors === 0`.
67: - `create.sh` function `finalize_scaffold_templates` replaces `[NAME]`, `[YYYY-MM-DD]`, `[Feature Name]` and `[###-feature-name]` and strips ` [template:...]` with `perl`. Function `ensure_template_source_near_top` moves the stamp line below the frontmatter. The stamp text, including its version, comes from the template.
68: - `templates/spec-kit-docs.json` lists a version per template, and `runtime/cli/tests/template-version-parity.vitest.ts` fails when a manifest version differs from the template stamp.
69: - `runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts` renders these templates and compares them with `runtime/cli/tests/snapshots/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts.snap`. Without `-u` it fails after conversion on four tests.
70: - The orchestrator reads every authored doc that is present. The shell rule reads only `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `decision-record.md`. This difference exists today and the plan keeps it for older docs (ADR-007).
71: 
72: ### Frozen definitions
73: 
74: **Hint.** A bracketed text that matches `\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]`. The slash lets the score cells `[/25]`, `[/20]` and `[/15]` count. Phase 1 counted with a letter-only start, so on the same Level 2 scaffold it saw 97 occurrences and this regex sees 101.
75: 
76: **Conversion rule.** The script `convert_hints.py` turns a hint into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ` followed by the hint text and `]`. The text keeps its case. It skips five cases:
77: 1. A line inside a fenced code block.
78: 2. Text inside an inline code span.
79: 3. Text followed directly by `(`, which is a link.
80: 4. The five scaffolder texts `NAME`, `Feature Name`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `###-feature-name` and `1/2/3/3+`, and any text that starts with `template:`. `create.sh` replaces or strips them, so a token there would stay in every scaffold.
81: 5. A text that already starts with `YOUR_VALUE_HERE`.
82: 
83: **Counts the conversion must give.** Converted per file: `spec.md.tmpl` 96, `plan.md.tmpl` 90, `tasks.md.tmpl` 7, `implementation-summary.md.tmpl` 11, `acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl` 10, so 214 in all. The total hint count of each file does not change, because a token is itself a hint under this regex. The bare hints left are exactly the ones in `tasks.md` T011.
84: 
85: **Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.
86: 
87: **Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.
88: 
89: **Lifecycle.**
90: 
91: | Doc | Status in `spec.md` | Unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` token | `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` | Strict result |
92: |-----|---------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------|
93: | Gate stamp | Draft | warning | error | passes when nothing else errors |
94: | Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |
95: | No gate stamp | any value | error | error | fails, as before |
96: 
97: Draft means the cell holds the word Draft, ignoring case, bold marks, backticks, outer quotes, trailing punctuation and repeated spaces. The first Status row of the metadata table counts.
98: 
99: ### Key Components
100: - **`convert_hints.py`**: the conversion tool, saved by `tasks.md` T004.
101: - **`replace_block.py`**: replaces the lines from a start marker up to an end marker, and refuses unless each marker occurs once. Used for the orchestrator.
102: - **`mutate.py`**: replaces one exact text that must occur once. Used for the mutation checks.
103: - **`apply_edits.py`**: applies old-text and new-text pairs to a doc, and refuses unless each old text occurs once.
104: - **`strict-census.mjs`**: validates every folder in a list with the orchestrator built in this checkout and prints one row per folder.
105: - **`suite_compare.py`**: compares two suite outputs and allows only the new test file and its tests.
106: - **`placeholder-token-gate.vitest.ts`**: the new test.
107: - **Conductor**: runs every task and reads every output.
108: - **Reviewer**: one read-only `cli-codex` review at phase close.
109: 
110: ### Data Flow
111: Templates are converted and stamped. A scaffold made from them carries tokens and the v2.3 stamp. The orchestrator reads the stamp and the spec status for each doc and returns pass, warn or error for `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The test drives the orchestrator through `validate.sh` and the shell rule through `bash -c`, and compares them.

404: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
405: 
406: ### ADR-001: Reuse the existing token and gate by the template stamp
407: 
408: **Status**: Accepted
409: 
410: **Context**: The token `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` is already an error in the validator and is already documented in `template-style-guide.md` section 3. A flag or an environment switch would need setting in every repo, and an external repo could not be expected to set it.
411: 
412: **Decision**: No new grammar. A doc stamped v2.3 or later gets the Draft lifecycle. Any other doc keeps its old verdict.
413: 
414: **Consequences**:
415: - The gate turns on by itself for each new scaffold and never for an old packet.
416: - A hand-written doc that copies a v2.3 stamp opts itself in. That is the intended meaning of the stamp.
417: 
418: **Alternatives Rejected**:
419: - An environment flag: it would have to be set in every external repo, and an unset flag is silent.
420: - Gating by packet creation date: dates are fragile across copies and renames, and the stamp already travels with the doc.
421: 
422: ### ADR-002: Draft means the word Draft, and a warning does not fail strict
423: 
424: **Status**: Accepted
425: 
426: **Context**: Planning commits must keep passing, as the rule `SCAFFOLD_NEVER_TOUCHED` already allows for a Draft. Other status words, such as Planned or In Progress, are real work states where a leftover hint is a defect.
427: 
428: **Decision**: Only the exact word Draft defers a token to a warning. Every other value, and a missing Status row, makes it an error. The orchestrator already treats a warning as advice, so strict still passes with warnings.
429: 
430: **Consequences**:
431: - A packet marked In Progress with tokens fails, which is the point of the gate.
432: - A packet with the status `Draft (phase 3)` counts as not Draft. The author writes `Draft`.
433: 
434: **Alternatives Rejected**:
435: - Treat every non-Complete status as Draft: a weak model that sets In Progress could then leave every hint for ever.
436: 
437: ### ADR-003: Record two defects in the post-edit scanner and leave the file alone
438: 
439: **Status**: Accepted
440: 
441: **Context**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-placeholders.sh` is the broad scan the post-edit hook runs. Two defects were observed with probe files. It skips only the lines that start a code fence and not the lines between fences, so a bracketed hint inside a fenced block exits 1. Its bracket class has no colon, so a line that holds a value token after the word Priority exits 0. After this phase the hook therefore stops reporting unfilled tokens in new packets.
442: 
443: **Decision**: This phase does not edit that file. It is a different script from the rule being changed, with a different caller, and the fix for the colon blind spot would change the hook verdict for existing packets that hold text such as `[SOURCE: ...]`. The conductor records the two defects in `goal.md` section 4 as follow-up rows with these probe commands, and raises them to the operator.
444: 
445: **Consequences**:
446: - The validator warning is the only signal for a Draft packet until the scanner is fixed.
447: - No existing hook verdict changes in this phase.
448: 
449: **Alternatives Rejected**:
450: - Add the colon to the bracket class here: it changes which existing packets the hook flags, with no test covering the scanner.
451: 
452: ### ADR-004: Convert with a script and keep the scaffolder's own placeholders
453: 
454: **Status**: Accepted
455: 
456: **Context**: By the frozen regex the five templates hold 254 bracketed hints. Of those, 214 are to convert, 38 are texts that `create.sh` replaces or strips and 2 sit inside an inline code span. A hand edit by a weak model would miss some and corrupt others.
457: 
458: **Decision**: `convert_hints.py` converts by the frozen rule and prints how many it changed. Counts before and after, and the list of bare texts left, are checked by commands.
459: 
460: **Consequences**:
461: - The result is the same on every run, and a second run changes nothing.
462: - A hint that the rule keeps but a later phase wants as a token needs a rule change, not a hand edit.
463: 
464: **Alternatives Rejected**:
465: - Convert by hand: error prone at this size.
466: - Convert the scaffolder's own placeholders too: every scaffold would then keep a token for the feature name and the date.
467: 
468: ### ADR-005: Accept the era report flip and raise it to the operator
469: 
470: **Status**: Accepted
471: 
472: **Context**: `template-version-parity.vitest.ts` forces the manifest version to equal the template stamp, so the manifest must say v2.3. `repo-era.mjs` marks a document `legacy` when its stamp differs from the manifest. Run against this repository with the two manifests, the report went from 16871 `new` and 2374 `legacy` markers to 1421 `new` and 17824 `legacy`. `/doctor:update check` treats a `legacy` count above zero as a pre-v4 signal, so a repo with none today would start showing it. The validator verdict for every packet is unchanged.
473: 
474: **Decision**: This phase does not edit `repo-era.mjs` or the doctor command. It records the measured counts and three options in `goal.md` section 4 and in the closing report: accept the flip, teach the era report that v2.2 is still a current stamp for old docs, or hold the manifest bump until the doctor signal is adjusted.
475: 
476: **Consequences**:
477: - The operator decides before a release carries the new templates to external repos.
478: - Decision D-b is met for the validator and open for the doctor signal.
479: 
480: **Alternatives Rejected**:
481: - Skip the manifest bump: the parity test would fail.
482: - Edit the era report here: it is outside the frozen file list and changes a doctor contract.
483: 
484: ### ADR-006: Record the upgrade-level token copy and leave it
485: 
486: **Status**: Accepted
487: 
488: **Context**: `upgrade-level.sh` renders sections from the templates into an older doc and does not touch the doc's template stamp. After this phase those sections arrive as tokens inside a doc that still says v2.2, and a token in a v2.2 doc is an error. Before this phase the same upgrade inserted bare hints that validated clean.
489: 
490: **Decision**: Not fixed here. The conductor records it as an operator item with the probe in `goal.md` section 4. The full suite includes `upgrade-level-sections.vitest.ts` and `test-upgrade-level.sh`, and `tasks.md` T017 reports whether either changed.
491: 
492: **Consequences**:
493: - An operator who upgrades an old packet to a higher level must fill the new sections or set the stamp.
494: - No existing packet changes, because the upgrade is an explicit action.
495: 
496: **Alternatives Rejected**:
497: - Stamp the upgraded doc v2.3: it would put a whole older doc under the new contract without anyone choosing that.
498: 
499: ### ADR-007: Update both implementations together and prove them with one test
500: 
501: **Status**: Accepted
502: 
503: **Context**: The orchestrator decides every real verdict. The shell rule is a mirror that a harness still drives. The two already differ in the docs they read.
504: 
505: **Decision**: Both get the same lifecycle in this phase. The shell rule reads `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md` and `goal.md` only when they carry the gate stamp, so older docs are scanned exactly as before. One test file runs both on the same folder and compares the result.
506: 
507: **Consequences**:
508: - For a doc with the gate stamp the two agree on pass, warn and error.
509: - The old difference in the docs read stays for older docs and is listed in `validation-rules.md`.
510: 
511: **Alternatives Rejected**:
512: - Update only the orchestrator: the mirror would drift on day one.

56: ## 3. ARCHITECTURE
57: 
58: ### Pattern
59: A stamp-gated lifecycle. The template stamp says which contract a doc was written under. The validator keeps the old strict verdict for any doc without the new stamp and applies the Draft lifecycle only to docs that carry it.
60: 
61: ### Facts read from the tree while this plan was written
62: 
63: - `validate.sh` runs the compiled `runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`, never the shell rules, for the rule `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The orchestrator lists it in `nativeRuleIds`, and `runRegistryShellRules` skips every rule in that set. The proof is the wording: a v2.3 scaffold validated in a scratch copy printed `unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet`, which is the new orchestrator message, and not the shell message.
64: - `validate.sh` exits 3 with the text `compiled validation orchestrator is stale` when `runtime/dist` is older than its source. So the TypeScript edit is invisible until `npm run build` runs under `runtime/`.
65: - `rules/check-placeholders.sh` still matters. The harness `runtime/cli/tests/test-validation-extended.sh` sources it in the category `Individual Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED (check-placeholders.sh)`, and its header says it mirrors the orchestrator.
66: - A warning does not fail strict. The orchestrator sets `passed: summary.errors === 0`.
67: - `create.sh` function `finalize_scaffold_templates` replaces `[NAME]`, `[YYYY-MM-DD]`, `[Feature Name]` and `[###-feature-name]` and strips ` [template:...]` with `perl`. Function `ensure_template_source_near_top` moves the stamp line below the frontmatter. The stamp text, including its version, comes from the template.
68: - `templates/spec-kit-docs.json` lists a version per template, and `runtime/cli/tests/template-version-parity.vitest.ts` fails when a manifest version differs from the template stamp.
69: - `runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts` renders these templates and compares them with `runtime/cli/tests/snapshots/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts.snap`. Without `-u` it fails after conversion on four tests.
70: - The orchestrator reads every authored doc that is present. The shell rule reads only `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `decision-record.md`. This difference exists today and the plan keeps it for older docs (ADR-007).
71: 
72: ### Frozen definitions
73: 
74: **Hint.** A bracketed text that matches `\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]`. The slash lets the score cells `[/25]`, `[/20]` and `[/15]` count. Phase 1 counted with a letter-only start, so on the same Level 2 scaffold it saw 97 occurrences and this regex sees 101.
75: 
76: **Conversion rule.** The script `convert_hints.py` turns a hint into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ` followed by the hint text and `]`. The text keeps its case. It skips five cases:
77: 1. A line inside a fenced code block.
78: 2. Text inside an inline code span.
79: 3. Text followed directly by `(`, which is a link.
80: 4. The five scaffolder texts `NAME`, `Feature Name`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `###-feature-name` and `1/2/3/3+`, and any text that starts with `template:`. `create.sh` replaces or strips them, so a token there would stay in every scaffold.
81: 5. A text that already starts with `YOUR_VALUE_HERE`.
82: 
83: **Counts the conversion must give.** Converted per file: `spec.md.tmpl` 96, `plan.md.tmpl` 90, `tasks.md.tmpl` 7, `implementation-summary.md.tmpl` 11, `acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl` 10, so 214 in all. The total hint count of each file does not change, because a token is itself a hint under this regex. The bare hints left are exactly the ones in `tasks.md` T011.
84: 
85: **Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.
86: 
87: **Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.
88: 
89: **Lifecycle.**
90: 
91: | Doc | Status in `spec.md` | Unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` token | `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` | Strict result |
92: |-----|---------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------|
93: | Gate stamp | Draft | warning | error | passes when nothing else errors |
94: | Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |
95: | No gate stamp | any value | error | error | fails, as before |
96: 
97: Draft means the cell holds the word Draft, ignoring case, bold marks, backticks, outer quotes, trailing punctuation and repeated spaces. The first Status row of the metadata table counts.
98: 
99: ### Key Components
100: - **`convert_hints.py`**: the conversion tool, saved by `tasks.md` T004.
101: - **`replace_block.py`**: replaces the lines from a start marker up to an end marker, and refuses unless each marker occurs once. Used for the orchestrator.
102: - **`mutate.py`**: replaces one exact text that must occur once. Used for the mutation checks.
103: - **`apply_edits.py`**: applies old-text and new-text pairs to a doc, and refuses unless each old text occurs once.
104: - **`strict-census.mjs`**: validates every folder in a list with the orchestrator built in this checkout and prints one row per folder.
105: - **`suite_compare.py`**: compares two suite outputs and allows only the new test file and its tests.
106: - **`placeholder-token-gate.vitest.ts`**: the new test.
107: - **Conductor**: runs every task and reads every output.
108: - **Reviewer**: one read-only `cli-codex` review at phase close.
109: 
110: ### Data Flow
111: Templates are converted and stamped. A scaffold made from them carries tokens and the v2.3 stamp. The orchestrator reads the stamp and the spec status for each doc and returns pass, warn or error for `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The test drives the orchestrator through `validate.sh` and the shell rule through `bash -c`, and compares them.

404: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
405: 
406: ### ADR-001: Reuse the existing token and gate by the template stamp
407: 
408: **Status**: Accepted
409: 
410: **Context**: The token `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` is already an error in the validator and is already documented in `template-style-guide.md` section 3. A flag or an environment switch would need setting in every repo, and an external repo could not be expected to set it.
411: 
412: **Decision**: No new grammar. A doc stamped v2.3 or later gets the Draft lifecycle. Any other doc keeps its old verdict.
413: 
414: **Consequences**:
415: - The gate turns on by itself for each new scaffold and never for an old packet.
416: - A hand-written doc that copies a v2.3 stamp opts itself in. That is the intended meaning of the stamp.
417: 
418: **Alternatives Rejected**:
419: - An environment flag: it would have to be set in every external repo, and an unset flag is silent.
420: - Gating by packet creation date: dates are fragile across copies and renames, and the stamp already travels with the doc.
421: 
422: ### ADR-002: Draft means the word Draft, and a warning does not fail strict
423: 
424: **Status**: Accepted
425: 
426: **Context**: Planning commits must keep passing, as the rule `SCAFFOLD_NEVER_TOUCHED` already allows for a Draft. Other status words, such as Planned or In Progress, are real work states where a leftover hint is a defect.
427: 
428: **Decision**: Only the exact word Draft defers a token to a warning. Every other value, and a missing Status row, makes it an error. The orchestrator already treats a warning as advice, so strict still passes with warnings.
429: 
430: **Consequences**:
431: - A packet marked In Progress with tokens fails, which is the point of the gate.
432: - A packet with the status `Draft (phase 3)` counts as not Draft. The author writes `Draft`.
433: 
434: **Alternatives Rejected**:
435: - Treat every non-Complete status as Draft: a weak model that sets In Progress could then leave every hint for ever.
436: 
437: ### ADR-003: Record two defects in the post-edit scanner and leave the file alone
438: 
439: **Status**: Accepted
440: 
441: **Context**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-placeholders.sh` is the broad scan the post-edit hook runs. Two defects were observed with probe files. It skips only the lines that start a code fence and not the lines between fences, so a bracketed hint inside a fenced block exits 1. Its bracket class has no colon, so a line that holds a value token after the word Priority exits 0. After this phase the hook therefore stops reporting unfilled tokens in new packets.
442: 
443: **Decision**: This phase does not edit that file. It is a different script from the rule being changed, with a different caller, and the fix for the colon blind spot would change the hook verdict for existing packets that hold text such as `[SOURCE: ...]`. The conductor records the two defects in `goal.md` section 4 as follow-up rows with these probe commands, and raises them to the operator.
444: 
445: **Consequences**:
446: - The validator warning is the only signal for a Draft packet until the scanner is fixed.
447: - No existing hook verdict changes in this phase.
448: 
449: **Alternatives Rejected**:
450: - Add the colon to the bracket class here: it changes which existing packets the hook flags, with no test covering the scanner.
451: 
452: ### ADR-004: Convert with a script and keep the scaffolder's own placeholders
453: 
454: **Status**: Accepted
455: 
456: **Context**: By the frozen regex the five templates hold 254 bracketed hints. Of those, 214 are to convert, 38 are texts that `create.sh` replaces or strips and 2 sit inside an inline code span. A hand edit by a weak model would miss some and corrupt others.
457: 
458: **Decision**: `convert_hints.py` converts by the frozen rule and prints how many it changed. Counts before and after, and the list of bare texts left, are checked by commands.
459: 
460: **Consequences**:
461: - The result is the same on every run, and a second run changes nothing.
462: - A hint that the rule keeps but a later phase wants as a token needs a rule change, not a hand edit.
463: 
464: **Alternatives Rejected**:
465: - Convert by hand: error prone at this size.
466: - Convert the scaffolder's own placeholders too: every scaffold would then keep a token for the feature name and the date.
467: 
468: ### ADR-005: Accept the era report flip and raise it to the operator
469: 
470: **Status**: Accepted
471: 
472: **Context**: `template-version-parity.vitest.ts` forces the manifest version to equal the template stamp, so the manifest must say v2.3. `repo-era.mjs` marks a document `legacy` when its stamp differs from the manifest. Run against this repository with the two manifests, the report went from 16871 `new` and 2374 `legacy` markers to 1421 `new` and 17824 `legacy`. `/doctor:update check` treats a `legacy` count above zero as a pre-v4 signal, so a repo with none today would start showing it. The validator verdict for every packet is unchanged.
473: 
474: **Decision**: This phase does not edit `repo-era.mjs` or the doctor command. It records the measured counts and three options in `goal.md` section 4 and in the closing report: accept the flip, teach the era report that v2.2 is still a current stamp for old docs, or hold the manifest bump until the doctor signal is adjusted.
475: 
476: **Consequences**:
477: - The operator decides before a release carries the new templates to external repos.
478: - Decision D-b is met for the validator and open for the doctor signal.
479: 
480: **Alternatives Rejected**:
481: - Skip the manifest bump: the parity test would fail.
482: - Edit the era report here: it is outside the frozen file list and changes a doctor contract.
483: 
484: ### ADR-006: Record the upgrade-level token copy and leave it
485: 
486: **Status**: Accepted
487: 
488: **Context**: `upgrade-level.sh` renders sections from the templates into an older doc and does not touch the doc's template stamp. After this phase those sections arrive as tokens inside a doc that still says v2.2, and a token in a v2.2 doc is an error. Before this phase the same upgrade inserted bare hints that validated clean.
489: 
490: **Decision**: Not fixed here. The conductor records it as an operator item with the probe in `goal.md` section 4. The full suite includes `upgrade-level-sections.vitest.ts` and `test-upgrade-level.sh`, and `tasks.md` T017 reports whether either changed.
491: 
492: **Consequences**:
493: - An operator who upgrades an old packet to a higher level must fill the new sections or set the stamp.
494: - No existing packet changes, because the upgrade is an explicit action.
495: 
496: **Alternatives Rejected**:
497: - Stamp the upgraded doc v2.3: it would put a whole older doc under the new contract without anyone choosing that.
498: 
499: ### ADR-007: Update both implementations together and prove them with one test
500: 
501: **Status**: Accepted
502: 
503: **Context**: The orchestrator decides every real verdict. The shell rule is a mirror that a harness still drives. The two already differ in the docs they read.
504: 
505: **Decision**: Both get the same lifecycle in this phase. The shell rule reads `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md` and `goal.md` only when they carry the gate stamp, so older docs are scanned exactly as before. One test file runs both on the same folder and compares the result.
506: 
507: **Consequences**:
508: - For a doc with the gate stamp the two agree on pass, warn and error.
509: - The old difference in the docs read stays for older docs and is listed in `validation-rules.md`.
510: 
511: **Alternatives Rejected**:
512: - Update only the orchestrator: the mirror would drift on day one.
513:

89: ```bash
90: cd "$WORKTREE"
91: cat > "$SC/tools/convert_hints.py" <<'PY'
92: # usage: convert_hints.py <template file>
93: # Rewrites the file in place and prints how many hints it turned into value tokens.
94: import re, sys
95: 
96: # A bracketed hint: a letter or slash, then at least two more characters, no nested brackets.
97: HINT = re.compile(r"\[(?!YOUR_VALUE_HERE)([A-Za-z/][^\]\[]{2,})\](?!\()")
98: # Text that create.sh replaces or strips at scaffold time must stay as written.
99: KEEP = ("NAME", "Feature Name", "YYYY-MM-DD", "###-feature-name", "1/2/3/3+")
100: CODE_SPAN = re.compile(r"`[^`]*`")
101: 
102: def convert_line(line):
103:     spans = [(m.start(), m.end()) for m in CODE_SPAN.finditer(line)]
104:     def inside_code(pos):
105:         return any(a <= pos < b for a, b in spans)
106:     def repl(m):
107:         body = m.group(1)
108:         if inside_code(m.start()) or body in KEEP or body.startswith("template:"):
109:             return m.group(0)
110:         counts["converted"] += 1
111:         return "[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: " + body + "]"
112:     return HINT.sub(repl, line)
113: 
114: path = sys.argv[1]
115: counts = {"converted": 0}
116: out, in_fence = [], False
117: for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n"):
118:     if re.match(r"^\s*(```|~~~)", line):
119:         in_fence = not in_fence
120:         out.append(line)
121:         continue
122:     out.append(line if in_fence else convert_line(line))
123: open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out))

125: PY

521: // Canonical spec-doc placeholder markers. Mirrors check-placeholders.sh

528: // A doc stamped with this template version or a later one ships every authoring

533: const TOKEN_GATE_MIN_MINOR = 3;

536: function carriesTokenGateStamp(content: string): boolean {
537:   for (const line of content.split(/\r?\n/u).slice(0, 70)) {
538:     const stamp = TEMPLATE_STAMP_RE.exec(line);
539:     if (!stamp) continue;
540:     const major = Number(stamp[1]);
541:     const minor = Number(stamp[2]);
542:     return major > TOKEN_GATE_MIN_MAJOR || (major === TOKEN_GATE_MIN_MAJOR && minor >= TOKEN_GATE_MIN_MINOR);

544:   return false;
545: }

547: function cleanStatusCell(cell: string): string {
548:   return cell.replace(/\*\*/gu, '').replace(/`/gu, '').trim();

551: // Reads the first Status row of spec.md's metadata table and reports whether its
552: // value is exactly Draft. Mirrors the shell classifier: quotes, case, trailing
553: // punctuation and repeated spaces do not change the answer, any other word does.
554: function specStatusIsDraft(folder: string): boolean {
555:   const spec = readIfExists(path.join(folder, 'spec.md'));
556:   if (!spec) return false;
557:   for (const line of spec.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
558:     if (!/^\s*\|/u.test(line)) continue;
559:     const cells = line.split('|');
560:     if (cells.length < 3) continue;
561:     if (cleanStatusCell(cells[1]).toLowerCase() !== 'status') continue;
562:     const value = cleanStatusCell(cells[2])
563:       .replace(/^["']/u, '')
564:       .replace(/["']$/u, '')
565:       .toLowerCase()
566:       .trim()
567:       .replace(/[\s.,;:!]+$/u, '')
568:       .replace(/\s+/gu, ' ');

570:   }

581:     const content = readIfExists(path.join(folder, docName));
582:     if (!content) continue;
583:     const tokenGated = carriesTokenGateStamp(content);
584:     const lines = content.split(/\r?\n/u);
585:     // Track fenced code blocks: a line starting with ``` toggles in_code and is
586:     // itself skipped, matching check-placeholders.sh awk behavior.
587:     let inCode = false;
588:     lines.forEach((line, index) => {
589:       if (/^\s*```/u.test(line)) {

608:     });

659: # Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED
660: # Severity: error
661: # Description: Detects unfilled spec-doc placeholders: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE:], [NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:] / [NEEDS CLARIFICATION:],
662: #   and a [template:...] provenance token left in a title line. Bracketed authoring hints such as [Decision Title]
663: #   are soft by design and belong to spec/check-placeholders.sh, the standalone report.
664: # Lifecycle: a doc whose SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE stamp is v2.3 or later ships every authoring hint as a
665: #   [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...] token. While spec.md has the Status Draft, an unfilled token in such a doc is a
666: #   warning. At any other status it is an error. A doc with an older stamp, or none, keeps the error it
667: #   always had. [NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:] is an error in every packet.
668: # Parity: mirrors the runtime orchestrator validatePlaceholders. Mustache {{...}} is NOT flagged
669: # (not canonical spec-doc placeholder syntax; legit spec-doc content uses it).
670: # The post-edit hook runs the broader bracket scan at spec/check-placeholders.sh
671: # instead; that one catches leftovers of upgrade-level, this one gates closure.
672: 
673: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
674: # 1. HELPERS
675: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
676: 
677: # Succeeds when the doc carries a SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE stamp of v2.3 or later
678: # within its first 70 lines. A doc with an older stamp, or none, fails.
679: carries_token_gate_stamp() {
680:     local filepath="$1"
681:     local stamp_line major minor
682:     stamp_line=$(head -n 70 "$filepath" 2>/dev/null | \
683:         grep -m1 -E '^[[:space:]]*<!--[[:space:]]*SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE:[^|>]*\|[[:space:]]*v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]*-->' || true)
684:     [[ -n "$stamp_line" ]] || return 1
685:     major=$(printf '%s' "$stamp_line" | sed -E 's/.*\|[[:space:]]*v([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+).*/\1/')
686:     minor=$(printf '%s' "$stamp_line" | sed -E 's/.*\|[[:space:]]*v([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+).*/\2/')
687:     if (( major > 2 )) || { (( major == 2 )) && (( minor >= 3 )); }; then
688:         return 0
689:     fi
690:     return 1
691: }
692: 
693: # Succeeds when the Status row of spec.md holds exactly the word Draft.
694: spec_status_is_draft() {
695:     local folder="$1"
696:     local value
697:     value="$(extract_status_table_value "$folder/spec.md")"
698:     [[ "$(speckit_status_trim "$value")" == "draft" ]]
699: }
700: 
701: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
702: # 2. INITIALIZATION
703: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
704: 
705: run_check() {
706:     local folder="$1"
707:     local level="$2"
708:     
709:     RULE_NAME="PLACEHOLDER_FILLED"
710:     RULE_STATUS="pass"
711:     RULE_MESSAGE=""
712:     RULE_DETAILS=()
713:     RULE_REMEDIATION=""
714:     
715:     local -a files=("spec.md" "plan.md" "tasks.md")
716:     [[ -f "$folder/decision-record.md" ]] && files+=("decision-record.md")
717:     # These three are read only when they carry the token-gate stamp, so a doc
718:     # with an older stamp is scanned exactly as it was before.
719:     files+=("acceptance-criteria.md" "implementation-summary.md" "goal.md")
720:     
721:     local -a found_placeholders=()
722:     local -a draft_tokens=()
723:     local draft_packet=false
724:     if spec_status_is_draft "$folder"; then
725:         draft_packet=true
726:     fi
727: 
728: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
729: # 3. VALIDATION LOGIC
730: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
731: 
732:     for file in "${files[@]}"; do
733:         local filepath="$folder/$file"
734:         [[ ! -f "$filepath" ]] && continue
735:         
736:         # Skip: scratch/, memory/, templates/
737:         if [[ "$filepath" == *"/scratch/"* ]] || \
738:            [[ "$filepath" == *"/memory/"* ]] || \
739:            [[ "$filepath" == *"/templates/"* ]]; then
740:             continue
741:         fi
742:         
743:         if type -t should_skip_path &>/dev/null; then
744:             if should_skip_path "$filepath"; then
745:                 continue
746:             fi
747:         fi
748: 
749:         local token_gated=false
750:         if carries_token_gate_stamp "$filepath"; then
751:             token_gated=true
752:         fi
753:         case "$file" in
754:             acceptance-criteria.md|implementation-summary.md|goal.md)
755:                 [[ "$token_gated" == true ]] || continue
756:                 ;;
757:         esac
758:         
759:         # Filter out fenced code blocks
760:         local filtered
761:         filtered=$(awk '
762:             BEGIN { in_code = 0 }
763:             /^```/ { in_code = !in_code; next }
764:             !in_code { print NR ":" $0 }
765:         ' "$filepath" 2>/dev/null)
766:         
767:         # Pattern 1: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE:] (skip inline backticks)
768:         # A token in a Draft packet is deferred to a warning when the doc carries
769:         # the token-gate stamp and the line holds no open question.
770:         while IFS= read -r match; do
771:             if [[ -n "$match" ]]; then
772:                 local linenum="${match%%:*}"
773:                 if [[ "$token_gated" == true && "$draft_packet" == true ]] && \
774:                    ! printf '%s' "$match" | grep -qE '\[NEEDS[_ ]CLARIFICATION:'; then
775:                     draft_tokens+=("$file:$linenum")
776:                 else
777:                     found_placeholders+=("$file:$linenum")
778:                 fi
779:             fi
780:         done < <(echo "$filtered" | grep -E '\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:' 2>/dev/null | \
781:                  grep -v '`\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:' | \
782:                  grep -v '\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:[^]]*\]`' || true)
783:         
784:         # Pattern 2: [NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:] / [NEEDS CLARIFICATION:] (underscore + space)
785:         # Strict superset-parity with the canonical orchestrator: both variants flagged.
786:         while IFS= read -r match; do
787:             if [[ -n "$match" ]]; then
788:                 local linenum="${match%%:*}"
789:                 found_placeholders+=("$file:$linenum")
790:             fi
791:         done < <(echo "$filtered" | grep -E '\[NEEDS[_ ]CLARIFICATION:' 2>/dev/null | \
792:                  grep -v '`\[NEEDS[_ ]CLARIFICATION:' | \
793:                  grep -v '\[NEEDS[_ ]CLARIFICATION:[^]]*\]`' || true)
794: 
795:         # Pattern 3: a template's [template:...] provenance token left in a title.
796:         # Scoped to title lines because that is the only place a scaffold ever
797:         # carried it; the scaffolder strips it, so a survivor is a hand-copied
798:         # template or a document older than that fix.
799:         while IFS= read -r match; do
800:             if [[ -n "$match" ]]; then
801:                 local linenum="${match%%:*}"
802:                 found_placeholders+=("$file:$linenum")
803:             fi
804:         done < <(echo "$filtered" | grep -E '^[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*title:.*\[template:' 2>/dev/null || true)
805:     done
806:     
807:     # Deduplicate (bash 3.2 compatible)
808:     local -a unique_placeholders=()
809:     local seen_list=""
810:     if [[ ${#found_placeholders[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
811:         for item in "${found_placeholders[@]}"; do
812:             if [[ "$seen_list" != *"|$item|"* ]]; then
813:                 seen_list="$seen_list|$item|"
814:                 unique_placeholders+=("$item")
815:             fi
816:         done
817:     fi
818: 
819:     local -a unique_draft_tokens=()
820:     seen_list=""
821:     if [[ ${#draft_tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
822:         for item in "${draft_tokens[@]}"; do
823:             if [[ "$seen_list" != *"|$item|"* ]]; then
824:                 seen_list="$seen_list|$item|"
825:                 unique_draft_tokens+=("$item")
826:             fi
827:         done
828:     fi
829: 
830: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
831: # 4. RESULTS
832: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
833: 
834:     local count=${#unique_placeholders[@]}
835:     local draft_count=${#unique_draft_tokens[@]}
836:     
837:     if [[ $count -gt 0 ]]; then
838:         RULE_STATUS="fail"
839:         RULE_MESSAGE="Found $count unfilled placeholder(s)"
840:         RULE_DETAILS=("${unique_placeholders[@]}")
841:         RULE_REMEDIATION="Replace [YOUR_VALUE_HERE:] and [NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:] / [NEEDS CLARIFICATION:] with actual values"
842:     elif [[ $draft_count -gt 0 ]]; then
843:         RULE_STATUS="warn"
844:         RULE_MESSAGE="Found $draft_count unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet"
845:         RULE_DETAILS=("${unique_draft_tokens[@]}")
846:         RULE_REMEDIATION="Replace each [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...] token with actual content before the status leaves Draft"
847:     else
848:         RULE_STATUS="pass"
849:         RULE_MESSAGE="No unfilled placeholders found"
850:     fi
851: }
852: 
853: # Exit codes:
854: #   0 - Success
855: SH
856: bash -n "$S/runtime/cli/rules/check-placeholders.sh" && echo SYNTAX_OK

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: Template Utils
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Template operations for spec-kit scripts.
# Source this file: source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/template-utils.sh"
#
# Functions:
# Get_level_templates_dir()  - Resolve template directory for a given level
# Copy_template()            - Copy template file with level-specific fallback
# Copy_templates_batch()      - Render several manifest templates in one Node process
# Resolve_level_contract()   - Print the private Level contract as JSON
# Level_contract_docs_from_json() - Print scaffolded docs from a contract JSON
#
# Compatibility: Bash 3.2+ (macOS default)
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Conditional strict mode — skipped when sourced to avoid breaking caller's error handling.
if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]; then
    set -euo pipefail
fi

# Guard against double-sourcing
[[ -n "${_TEMPLATE_UTILS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_TEMPLATE_UTILS_LOADED=1

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Get level-specific templates directory path.
# Maps documentation level (1, 2, 3, 3+) to the appropriate folder.
#
# Usage: dir=$(get_level_templates_dir "2" "/path/to/templates")
# Args:
# $1 - Documentation level: 1, 2, 3, or 3+
# $2 - Base templates directory path
# Returns: Prints resolved directory path to stdout
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
get_level_templates_dir() {
    local level="$1"
    local base_dir="$2"
    case "$level" in
        1) printf '%s\n' "$base_dir/level-1" ;;
        2) printf '%s\n' "$base_dir/level-2" ;;
        3) printf '%s\n' "$base_dir/level-3" ;;
        "3+"|4) printf '%s\n' "$base_dir/level-3+" ;;
        *) printf '%s\n' "$base_dir/level-1" ;;  # Default fallback
    esac
}

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Copy a template file to a destination directory with fallback.
# Tries level-specific folder first, then falls back to base templates.
# Missing required templates fail closed.
#
# Consolidated from create.sh's copy_template() and copy_subfolder_template()
# Which were near-identical (only differed in destination directory).
#
# Usage: copy_template "spec.md" "/dest/dir" "/level/templates" "/base/templates" [dest_name]
# Args:
# $1 - Template filename (e.g., "spec.md")
# $2 - Destination directory (e.g., "$FEATURE_DIR" or "$SUBFOLDER_PATH")
# $3 - Level-specific templates directory
# $4 - Base templates directory (fallback)
# $5 - (Optional) Destination filename if different from template name
# Returns: Prints the created filename to stdout (for tracking in CREATED_FILES)
# Exit: Non-zero when rendering, writing, or template lookup fails
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
copy_template() {
    local template_name="$1"
    local dest_dir="$2"
    local level_or_dir="$3"
    local base_templates_dir="$4"
    local dest_name="${5:-$template_name}"
    local render_level
    render_level="$(_normalize_template_level "$level_or_dir")"
    local dest_path="$dest_dir/$dest_name"
    local template_path

    if ! _validate_contract_doc_name "$template_name" || ! _validate_contract_doc_name "$dest_name"; then
        echo "Error: invalid template document name for Level $render_level" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    if ! _ensure_dest_within_dir "$dest_dir" "$dest_path"; then
        echo "Error: template destination escapes target folder for Level $render_level" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    template_path="$(_manifest_template_path "$template_name" "$render_level" "$base_templates_dir")"

    if [[ -f "$template_path" ]]; then
        local renderer tmp_path
        renderer="$(_inline_gate_renderer_path)"
        tmp_path="$(mktemp "${dest_path}.tmp.XXXXXX")"
        if "$renderer" --level "$render_level" "$template_path" > "$tmp_path"; then
            :
        else
            local render_status=$?
            rm -f "$tmp_path"
            return "$render_status"
        fi
        if ! mv "$tmp_path" "$dest_path"; then
            local move_status=$?
            rm -f "$tmp_path"
            return "$move_status"
        fi
        printf '%s\n' "$dest_name"
    else
        echo "Error: required template document missing for Level $render_level: $template_name" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

copy_templates_batch() {
    local docs="$1"
    local dest_dir="$2"
    local render_level="$3"
    local base_templates_dir="$4"
    local renderer
    renderer="$(_inline_gate_renderer_path)"

    local template_paths=()
    local doc_names=()
    local template_name template_path
    while IFS= read -r template_name; do
        [[ -z "$template_name" ]] && continue
        if ! _validate_contract_doc_name "$template_name"; then
            echo "Error: invalid template document name for Level $render_level" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        template_path="$(_manifest_template_path "$template_name" "$render_level" "$base_templates_dir")"
        if [[ ! -f "$template_path" ]]; then
            echo "Error: required template document missing for Level $render_level: $template_name" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        if ! _ensure_dest_within_dir "$dest_dir" "$dest_dir/$template_name"; then
            echo "Error: template destination escapes target folder for Level $render_level" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        template_paths+=("$template_path")
        doc_names+=("$template_name")
